title: Ribbon runs: First qualifying slip
summary: A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
A sticking key leaves repeated marks across a typewriter ribbon's inspection strip. Alma needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement ribbonRunsFirstQualifyingSlip(line, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: String runs. A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
The line contains ASCII characters; the only word separator is a space.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with string runs. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [1,1,2,1,1,3,1,1,1]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives 3.
The derived sequence is [2,1,1,2]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives 2.
The derived sequence is []. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives -1.
